clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A family member accompanies a client to an outpatient oncology clinic and reports a new cough and nasal congestion. Which action by clinic staff is appropriate?

options.A: Provide a facemask and ask the symptomatic family member not to enter patient-care areas, encouraging waiting outside or deferring the visit.
options.B: Allow entry into the treatment area without additional measures unless a respiratory infection has been laboratory confirmed.
options.C: Permit entry if the family member avoids touching the client and sits one chair away from other people.
options.D: Delay respiratory precautions until fever develops because cough and congestion alone do not warrant source-control measures.

semantic_correction.rationale: CDC's outpatient oncology infection-control plan applies respiratory-hygiene measures to patients, family members, caregivers, and visitors with symptoms such as cough or congestion. Symptomatic persons should be provided a facemask, and accompanying persons with respiratory symptoms should not enter patient-care areas and should be encouraged to wait outside the facility. Current CDC viral-respiratory guidance also recommends that symptomatic visitors defer non-urgent routine visits and wear a mask while in the facility. These measures are based on symptoms and do not require a confirmed diagnosis or fever. Therefore option A is correct.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Apply respiratory source-control and visitor-separation measures to symptomatic visitors in outpatient oncology settings before they enter patient-care areas.
semantic_correction.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: Symptomatic accompanying persons or visitors in outpatient oncology should receive source-control measures such as a facemask and should not enter patient-care areas; non-urgent visits should be deferred when appropriate.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed the 'only' distractor cue, shortened the correct answer, and anchored visitor management to symptom-based CDC source-control and separation guidance rather than requiring diagnostic confirmation or fever.

audit_findings_append.finding: The original construct was correct but contained an absolute distractor. The revised item directly tests symptom-based visitor source control and patient-area separation with balanced alternatives.

option_audit.A: Correct. It follows CDC masking and separation guidance for symptomatic accompanying persons.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Respiratory source-control measures are symptom based and do not require laboratory confirmation.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Symptomatic accompanying persons should not enter patient-care areas; one-chair spacing is not an adequate substitute.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Cough and congestion are sufficient respiratory symptoms to trigger source-control measures even without fever.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone combines the exact outpatient-oncology masking and exclusion-from-patient-care-area actions recommended by CDC.
cueing_check: All four choices are visitor-management actions of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
